Central Nervous System
Anatomy
Cerebellum & 4th Ventricle

This lesson covers the internal architecture of the cerebellum — its cortex, medullary core, and the four pairs of deep cerebellar nuclei — along with the three cerebellar peduncles that link it to the brainstem. It then moves to the fourth ventricle: its shape and position, its lateral boundaries, its three-part roof, and the surface landmarks on its floor produced by underlying cranial nerve nuclei. Finally, it covers how the ventricle communicates with the rest of the CSF pathway, drains through its three foramina into the subarachnoid space, and is supplied with CSF by its own choroid plexus.

Internal Structure of the Cerebellum

The cerebellum consists internally of an outer cortex and a center medullary core:

  • Outer cortex: a thin layer of gray matter that covers the cerebellar folia.
  • Center medullary core: formed of white matter that extends into the cerebellar folia in a branching pattern called arbor vitae. This white matter core is continuous anteriorly with the three cerebellar peduncles.

Cerebellar Nuclei

These are masses of gray matter embedded in the white matter core. They are four pairs, arranged from medial to lateral:

NucleusPosition & features
Fastigial nucleusThe most medially situated of the four pairs.
Globosus & Emboliform nucleiTwo small nuclei situated between the fastigial and dentate nuclei. Called together nucleus interpositus, forming one functional unit.
Dentate nucleusThe most laterally situated and the largest of the cerebellar nuclei; appears as a crenated sac that opens anteromedially.

Cerebellar Peduncles

These are masses of white matter that connect the cerebellum with the brainstem; they contain both afferent and efferent fibers.

PeduncleConnects withMain fibersOther notes
Inferior cerebellar peduncle Medulla Olivocerebellar & cerebellolivary fibers Forms the upper lateral boundary of the 4th ventricle
Middle cerebellar peduncle Pons Pontocerebellar fibers The largest of the three peduncles
Superior cerebellar peduncle Midbrain Efferent cerebellar fibers to red nucleus & thalamus Forms the lower lateral boundary of the 4th ventricle

Fourth Ventricle

Shape & Position

  • Shape: a tent-like cavity.
  • Position: in front of the cerebellum, behind the pons and upper part of the medulla oblongata.

Boundaries

Lateral boundaries (from above downward):

  • Superior cerebellar peduncle
  • Inferior cerebellar peduncle
  • Cuneate tubercle
  • Gracile tubercle

Roof (posterior wall) — divided into three parts:

Part of roofStructure
Upper thirdSuperior medullary velum — a thin sheet of white matter extending between the superior cerebellar peduncles.
Middle thirdWhite core of the cerebellum.
Lower thirdInferior medullary velum — a thin layer of ependyma, covered by pia mater.

The lower part of the roof is invaginated by the choroid plexus, which secretes CSF, and presents 3 foramina for CSF drainage into the subarachnoid space: a large median aperture, the foramen of Magendie, and two lateral apertures, the foramina of Luschka.

Floor of the Fourth Ventricle

The floor is formed by the posterior aspect of the pons and upper medulla. The stria medullaris (transverse fibers) separates the pontine part from the medullary part, and a median sulcus divides the floor into right and left symmetrical halves.

RegionLandmarkProduced by / description
Pontine partMedial eminenceLongitudinal elevation on either side of the median sulcus.
Facial colliculusSwelling at the lower end of the medial eminence, produced by the facial nerve looping around the abducent nucleus.
Superior foveaGroove lateral to the facial colliculus.
Vestibular areaLateral to the superior fovea; overlies the superior, lateral & medial vestibular nuclei.
Medullary partInferior foveaAn inverted V-shaped groove.
Hypoglossal trigoneClose to the midline; produced by the hypoglossal nucleus.
Vagal / Vestibular trigonesVagal trigone: between the two limbs of the inferior fovea, produced by the dorsal nucleus of vagus. Vestibular trigone: situated laterally, produced by the inferior vestibular nucleus.

Angles, Recesses & Communications

  • Angles: the ventricular cavity has 4 angles — a superior, an inferior, and 2 lateral angles.
  • Recesses: 3 extensions of the cavity — 1 cerebellar recess (posterior extension into the cerebellar white core) and 2 lateral recesses (lateral extensions of the lateral angles).
  • The foramina of Luschka each open at the roof of the lateral end of the lateral recesses, draining into the subarachnoid space.

Communications of the 4th ventricle:

  • Above: with the third ventricle, through the aqueduct of the midbrain (of Sylvius).
  • Below: with the central canal of the closed medulla.
  • With the subarachnoid space: through the foramen of Magendie and the foramina of Luschka.

Choroid Plexus of the Fourth Ventricle

  • A tuft of capillaries that projects into the cavity of the 4th ventricle through the lower part of its roof.
  • It receives its blood supply from a branch of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery.

Key Points / Quick Review

Cerebellar Nuclei (medial → lateral)

  • Fastigial — most medial
  • Globosus & Emboliform — together = nucleus interpositus
  • Dentate — most lateral, largest, crenated sac

Cerebellar Peduncles

  • Inferior → medulla; upper lateral boundary of 4th ventricle
  • Middle → pons; largest peduncle
  • Superior → midbrain; lower lateral boundary of 4th ventricle

4th Ventricle Shape & Boundaries

  • Tent-like; in front of cerebellum, behind pons/upper medulla
  • Lateral boundaries: sup. & inf. cerebellar peduncles, cuneate & gracile tubercles

Roof (3 thirds)

  • Upper: superior medullary velum
  • Middle: white core of cerebellum
  • Lower: inferior medullary velum

Floor Landmarks

  • Pontine: facial colliculus (facial nerve around abducent nucleus), vestibular area
  • Medullary: hypoglossal trigone, vagal trigone, vestibular trigone

CSF Drainage & Communications

  • Above: aqueduct of Sylvius (to 3rd ventricle)
  • Below: central canal
  • To subarachnoid space: foramen of Magendie + foramina of Luschka
  • Choroid plexus supplied by posterior inferior cerebellar artery
